input.rationale: Leaves one sourced, unexecuted lead for whoever continues, rather than closing the run on a claim the evidence does not yet carry. Reading the follower's prepare handler (follower.rs 13-51) shows a second place where a prefix below the compacted index can be asked of the storage, this time by the replica itself: when the accepted round the follower holds is greater than the leader's reported one it answers with create_log_sync(prep.decided_idx, prep.decided_idx), and when the rounds are equal and its accepted index is greater it answers with create_log_sync(prep.accepted_idx, prep.decided_idx); both pass a number taken from the leader's Prepare as the common prefix into its own storage. For an entry type without snapshots that prefix reaches get_suffix, whose subtraction of the trimmed index is unguarded, so a follower whose compacted index is above the number the new leader reports would abort inside its own message handling; for the snapshot-capable type the same call takes the Complete-snapshot branch instead, which is why the probe has to be run with both entry types. Reachability needs a newly elected leader that reports a decided or accepted index below a follower's compacted index, which is a legal history - a follower that learned a decision its later leader missed - and it is exactly the shape this audit has already driven for the drift, so the probe is cheap to add to the existing harness rather than a new fixture. Recorded as a new question on the drift investigation with its hypothesis, conditions and discriminator, and as a knowledge entry for the handler branch itself; nothing was executed, no account or gap changed, and the existing accounts keep their current conclusions and limits.

investigations.question: Can a follower's own answer to a Prepare ask its storage for a prefix below the index it has already compacted to, when the newly elected leader reports a decided or accepted index smaller than that follower's compacted index? The follower builds its Promise's LogSync from the leader's numbers - create_log_sync(prep.decided_idx, prep.decided_idx) when its accepted round is greater, and create_log_sync(prep.accepted_idx, prep.decided_idx) when the rounds are equal and its accepted index is greater - and create_log_sync reads a suffix from the follower's own storage at that prefix.
investigations.hypothesis: For an entry type whose Snapshot is NoSnapshot, such a Promise aborts the follower inside handle_prepare, because create_log_sync's non-snapshot branch calls get_suffix(common_prefix_idx) and the shipped in-memory storage subtracts its trimmed index from that value without a guard; for the snapshot-capable type the same call takes the snapshot branch (the follower's own decided index is above the prefix) and builds a Complete snapshot instead, so the two entry types differ exactly as they did in the storage-level probe.
investigations.discriminator: A run in which a follower holds a compacted index above the decided or accepted index a newly elected leader reports in its Prepare, sampled with both entry types: the decisive observation is whether the follower's Promise is built and sent (with the Panic reported through the harness's guard if not), together with the leader's reported numbers and the follower's compacted index at that moment. Reachability is the part that needs the run: the shape requires a leader that missed a decision the follower received, which the harness can produce by cutting the future leader off while the older leader decides and then electing it.

knowledge.statement: A follower's Promise builds its LogSync from the leader's Prepare rather than from its own log: when its accepted round is greater than prep.n_accepted it calls create_log_sync(prep.decided_idx, prep.decided_idx), and when the rounds are equal and its accepted index is greater it calls create_log_sync(prep.accepted_idx, prep.decided_idx). Both numbers come from the new leader, so a follower whose own compacted index is above either of them asks its own storage for a suffix below its trimmed index; for a NoSnapshot entry type that reaches get_suffix and its unguarded subtraction, while for a snapshot-capable type the call takes the Complete-snapshot branch because the follower's own decided index lies above the prefix.
knowledge.conditions: Reached in the follower's handle_prepare when the preconditions above hold, i.e. a re-promising follower that is more up to date in its accepted round or index than the leader that prepared it, which is legal whenever the leader missed a decision or an accept round that the follower learned. Read from follower.rs 13-51 together with create_log_sync (mod.rs 405-432), the shipped storage's unguarded subtraction and the snapshot branch's own bound; not executed in this run, and the abort is therefore a sourced expectation rather than an observation.

investigations.question: When a replica that has already accepted its configuration's StopSign is re-synchronized by the leader (PrepareReq -> Prepare -> Promise -> AcceptSync, e.g. after a re-established connection), does its reported accepted index stay within its actual log content, so that the StopSign keeps being observable as decided (decided index == accepted index) and the decided log keeps being readable?
investigations.hypothesis: No. create_log_sync passes the follower's accepted index (which already counts its stored StopSign as one index) as LogSync.sync_idx; sync_log sets accepted_idx = sync_idx + suffix.len() and then adds 1 again because the LogSync carries the StopSign, so the re-synchronized replica's accepted index becomes one larger than its log content while its decided index stays at the real StopSign position. The replica then reports the inflated index in Accepted, so a write quorum of inflated reports lets the leader set a decided index beyond the entries it can read.
investigations.discriminator: Nothing that a further source reading would change; only further executions. Both variants the earlier discriminator named are settled by source: a peer receiving a forwarded Compaction::Snapshot compacts to the requested index only when that index is within its own decided index (and then builds its own snapshot from its own range), otherwise try_snapshot refuses it with UndecidedIndex and handle_compaction discards the error, so the peer keeps its state rather than mirroring the leader's loss (knowledge 69d9dfec8808400f931ca863a93167c3-knowledge-0, material mod.rs 217-227); and the trim path cannot raise a compacted index above a live replica's reported accepted index at all, because its bound is the minimum over a per-node initialised vector. result.summary: Leaves the run with one sourced, unexecuted lead rather than closing on an unsupported claim. Reading the follower's prepare handler shows a second place where a prefix below the compacted index can be asked of the storage, this time by the replica itself: when the follower's accepted round exceeds the leader's reported one it answers with create_log_sync(prep.decided_idx, prep.decided_idx), and when the rounds are equal and its accepted index is greater it answers with create_log_sync(prep.accepted_idx, prep.decided_idx), so both numbers come from the new leader's Prepare and are used as the common prefix into the follower's own storage. Reachability needs a legal history in which a newly elected leader missed a decision the follower learned, and the existing harness can produce that by cutting the future leader off while the older leader decides and then electing it, so the lead is cheap to test rather than a new fixture. Recorded as a new question on the drift investigation - with the hypothesis, the cited handler, storage and snapshot material, and a discriminator naming the decisive observation and the reachability step - and as a knowledge entry for the handler branch itself, both clearly marked as sourced expectations rather than observations. Nothing else changed: every other account, gap and discriminator keeps its current conclusion and limits, and no execution was requested, so the remaining work is explicitly a probe someone can pick up rather than an unresolved claim.

investigations.discriminator: Nothing that a further source reading would change; only further executions. Both variants the earlier discriminator named are settled by source: a peer receiving a forwarded Compaction::Snapshot compacts to the requested index only when that index is within its own decided index (and then builds its own snapshot from its own range), otherwise try_snapshot refuses it with UndecidedIndex and handle_compaction discards the error, so the peer keeps its state rather than mirroring the leader's loss (knowledge 69d9dfec8808400f931ca863a93167c3-knowledge-0, material mod.rs 217-227); and the trim path cannot raise a compacted index above a live replica's reported accepted index at all, because its bound is the minimum over a per-node initialised vector. knowledge.statement: A forwarded compaction is applied by each peer independently and its outcome is discarded: SequencePaxos::handle_compaction calls the node's own trim or snapshot path for a Compaction::Trim or Compaction::Snapshot and ignores the returned error, so a peer compacts to the leader's index only when that index is within its own decided index (snapshot) or at or below its own minimum recorded accepted index (trim). A peer whose own decided index lies below a forwarded snapshot index refuses it with UndecidedIndex, the error is discarded and the peer stays exactly as it was; a peer whose decided index covers the index compacts to it and builds its own snapshot from its own storage range, which can be empty when its log holds nothing above its own compacted index.

knowledge.statement: A follower's Promise builds its LogSync from the leader's Prepare rather than from its own log: when its accepted round is greater than prep.n_accepted it calls create_log_sync(prep.decided_idx, prep.decided_idx), and when the rounds are equal and its accepted index is greater it calls create_log_sync(prep.accepted_idx, prep.decided_idx). Both numbers come from the new leader, so a follower whose own compacted index is above either of them asks its own storage for a suffix below its trimmed index; for a NoSnapshot entry type that reaches get_suffix and its unguarded subtraction, while for a snapshot-capable type the call takes the Complete-snapshot branch because the follower's own decided index lies above the prefix.
